name: Global Steering Systems
old_description: Global Steering Systems is the world’s leading manufacturer of steering components for automotive giants like Ford Motor Company, Jeep, Lucid Motors, and General Motors, to name a few. With a decades-long track record of excellence and production capabilities in North America, Asia Pacific, and Europe, GSS designs and manufactures “must-have” products for ensuring driver safety and satisfaction the world over—now and in the years ahead.
about:
Global Steering Systems is headquartered in Watertown, Connecticut. The company was founded more than four decades ago as an independent, privately held business and remains under private ownership.

The company reports a decades-long track record of excellence and production capabilities across North America, Asia Pacific, and Europe. It designs and manufactures steering components including column shafts, U-joints, center-mounted support bearings, and complex intermediate shafts for column-drive and rack-drive applications. A proprietary high-performance spline slider is produced in-house. Operations are supported by a full-service test lab that validates products at every manufacturing step and a full-service engineering group that handles design, analysis, risk assessment, prototyping, and validation testing. GSS operates facilities in Connecticut (headquarters, R&D, and manufacturing), Michigan (sales and support), Changshu, China (manufacturing, sales, and support), Opole, Poland (manufacturing, R&D, sales, and support), and Ponta Grossa, Brazil (sales and support).

GSS serves the automotive industry, supplying light- and heavy-duty vehicle platforms. Its customer base includes major OEMs such as Ford Motor Company, Jeep, Lucid Motors, and General Motors.

The company emphasizes rigorous testing at every production stage, cross-functional product development teams, and the ability to combine innovative designs with off-the-shelf components to respond quickly to market demand. It states that these capabilities set a new global standard for steering systems.
